docs.title: Unity Game — Dev Log
docs.text:
2D card roguelike prototype, Slay the Spire style, built in Unity 6.3 (URP 2D).

This site is the work log: one page per live coding session, with what was done, what was learned and which files changed.

Published site

The log is online at https://albertacedo.github.io/Unity-Game/ and is updated with python -m mkdocs gh-deploy at the end of every session.

docs.text: Item Status Playable loop ✅ map → combat → reward → map Map ⚠️ radial: centre, 8 rings, 4-7 bosses, configurable fog, zoom/pan and safe connections; being redesigned (reveal radius and backtracking) Combat ✅ turns, energy, block, Vulnerable, multi-enemy with targeting Content 10 cards · 2 enemies, 2 packs and 1 boss, and relic/event tables (still inert), all in editable CSV Test tools ✅ F1 panel, deck view, combat feedback, tools/compile-check.ps1 Content tools ✅ Prototype → Content (CSV) window and tools/content-check Gold ⚠️ shown but cannot be spent (shop pending) Audio / art ❌ placeholder

docs.title: How to run it
docs.text:
1. Open the project with Unity 6000.3.26f1.
  2. Open Assets/Scenes/Prototype.unity.
  3. Press Play.
  4. In game: F1 opens the development panel.

docs.title: Stack
docs.text:
• Unity 6000.3.26f1 (Unity 6.3), URP 2D
  • New Input System (no legacy)
  • UI: UGUI + TextMeshPro, built from code
  • Content: cards, enemies, relics and events in CSV (Assets/Resources/Content/), read by ContentDatabase

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The whole game is built from code: the scene only holds a Game object with the GameManager component. There are no prefabs and no hand-assembled screens. Content, on the other hand, is data: four CSV tables in Assets/Resources/Content (see Content in CSV).

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
GameManager.Awake()
  ├─ creates Canvas + EventSystem
  ├─ creates DevPanel (F1)
  └─ StartNewRun(seed)
        └─ ShowMap() → MapScreen
              └─ node click → StartCombat() / ShowRest() / ShowPlaceholder()
                    └─ CombatScreen → OnCombatFinished()
                          ├─ victory → ShowReward() → Advance() → ShowMap()
                          └─ defeat  → ShowEnd()

GameManager.Clear() destroys every child of Screens before drawing the next screen. The layers that must survive (the DevPanel) hang off the Canvas, not off Screens.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File Responsibility Scripts/GameManager.cs Entry point, screen switching, debug helpers Scripts/Run/RunState.cs HP, gold, seed, map and deck (what survives between rooms) Scripts/Mapgen/MapGenerator.cs Seeded, deterministic radial map Scripts/Mapgen/MapLayout.cs Geometry shared by map and screen (radius, angle and ellipse) Scripts/Combat/CombatSession.cs Combat rules (turns, energy, damage, block, target) Scripts/Combat/EnemyInstance.cs State of one enemy inside a fight (HP, block, Vulnerable, intent) Scripts/Content/ContentCsv.cs CSV table format: reading, writing and validation Scripts/Content/ContentDatabase.cs Loads Resources/Content/*.csv and caches them Scripts/Content/CardLibrary.cs Facade: starting deck, reward pool and encounters Scripts/Data/CardData.cs Card, effects and text generated from the effects Scripts/Data/EnemyData.cs Enemy, role (solo/group/boss) and intent queue Scripts/Data/RelicData.cs Relic (catalogue; the system does not exist yet) Scripts/Data/EventData.cs Event and options (catalogue; the screen does not exist yet) Editor/ContentWindow.cs Prototype → Content (CSV) window for editing the tables Scripts/UI/UIFactory.cs Helpers to build UI from code Scripts/UI/MapScreen.cs Map, nodes and connections Scripts/UI/CombatScreen.cs Combat, hand, visual feedback Scripts/UI/RewardScreen.cs Pick 3 cards Scripts/UI/SimpleScreens.cs Rest, placeholder and end of run Scripts/UI/DeckScreen.cs Overlay with the whole deck Scripts/DevPanel.cs Test panel (F1)

docs.title: Implemented rules
docs.text:
• Content: cards, enemies, relics and events are data, not code. They live in Assets/Resources/Content/*.csv, are loaded once by ContentDatabase and there is no content .asset at all. Format, rules and editing workflow are in Content in CSV.
  • Map: radial and deterministic per seed. A Start node at the centre, 8 rings (6 room rings + 1 boss ring) and 4-7 bosses on the outer ring. Lateral connections within the room rings are generated with 55% probability and are always drawn as straight lines. 35% of the rooms may also have a diagonal connection to the neighbouring angular branch of the next ring. Diagonals are rejected if they cross a road, touch another node's rectangle or pass within 8 units of its visual edge.
  • Room type: ring 1 is always combat; rings 2-5 roll 50% combat, 15% rest, 10% shop and 25% event. Bosses are always bosses, and Elite is not generated yet.
  • Connections: between two neighbouring rings, each room links to the room (or boss) closest in angle. The map ends up split into wedges centred on the small ring. Rooms on the same ring are joined with straight lines, and the ring just before the bosses is complete.
  • Geometry: MapLayout is the only source of positions. The map is an ellipse 1.45 times wider than tall, to make the most of the 16:9 screen. Each boss sits on the angular centre of its rooms, so that no edge leaves its ring (an edge steeper than ~35° would enter the inner ring and cross roads).
  • Zoom and pan: mouse wheel (or the + / − buttons) to zoom between 60% and 220%, drag with the right or middle button to move the map. The map is clipped to its area (RectMask2D), so it never covers the HUD, and RESET VIEW returns to the initial state. Rooms can be clicked at any zoom level. While an overlay is open (the deck), MapScreen.Update ignores wheel and drag: scrolling the cards must not move the map behind.
  • Movement: every choice moves exactly one node and you can walk in both directions. Visited rooms do not repeat content, but you can cross them to get back to a branch. Room types only reveal themselves within the configured radius (1-5, 1 by default); bosses are visible from the start. The topology and the roads are always visible. The F1 panel lets you try fog, reveal radius 1-5 and backtracking without restarting. There are no provisions yet: first we check whether movement and single-use content already create enough commitment.
  • Combat: 3 energy per turn, draw 5, block resets every turn.
  • Multi-enemy: 1 normal enemy or a pack of 2 weak variants. Each enemy has its own HP, block, Vulnerable and intent queue; the fight ends when they all fall.
  • Target: attack cards hit Target; when it dies, targeting moves to the next living enemy. DamageAll (Cleave) hits every living enemy.
  • Vulnerable: multiplies incoming damage by 1.5, one counter per enemy (and one for the player) that drops by 1 at the end of the round.
  • Run: 72 HP, 99 gold (still unused).

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: I want to… Where I touch it Add a card Resources/Content/cards.csv (or the Prototype → Content window): one row Add an enemy Resources/Content/enemies.csv: one row with its role Add an effect EffectKind (in CardData) + the switch in CombatSession.ApplyEffects + a field in EnemyInstance if it is a status + the name in ContentCsv Add a relic or an event relics.csv / events.csv; the game system still has to be written Add a screen GameManager.ScreenKind + a ShowX() + a class in UI/ Change how an element looks UIFactory (affects every screen at once)

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
• tools/compile-check.ps1 compiles Assets/Scripts and Assets/Editor against the DLLs in Library/ using the .NET SDK, without opening Unity. It is the first verification step; after that you still need to check the console and try Play mode.
  • tools/content-check/ validates the content CSVs without opening Unity: same parser, same rules and a round-trip test of every table.
  • Prototype → Content (CSV) is the content editing window inside the Editor.
  • .opencode/skills/ holds the agent's reusable instructions. There are two kinds: the project ones (UI from code, balance, verification, effects: what only this repo knows) and the external ones, copied from the skills.sh catalogue with the source and date in the footer. At the end of every session both are reviewed: the project ones are updated, and for general knowledge an external skill is looked up before writing a new one. See External skills.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Prototype namespace, sub-namespaces per subsystem (Prototype.UI, Prototype.Combat…).
  • One public MonoBehaviour per file, named after the file.
  • [SerializeField] private fields; nothing public in the Inspector.
  • New Input System always (Keyboard.current, never Input.GetKey).
  • .meta files are generated by Unity: never by hand.

docs.title: Content in CSV
docs.text:
Cards, enemies, relics and events are not ScriptableObjects or .asset files: they live in four CSV tables inside the project and the game loads them on startup.

The goal is to be able to design content in a spreadsheet (or in a Unity window) without touching code or creating assets by hand.

docs.title: Where everything is
docs.text:
Piece File Cards Assets/Resources/Content/cards.csv Enemies Assets/Resources/Content/enemies.csv Relics Assets/Resources/Content/relics.csv Events Assets/Resources/Content/events.csv Parser and format Assets/Scripts/Content/ContentCsv.cs Loading into the game Assets/Scripts/Content/ContentDatabase.cs Editing window Assets/Editor/ContentWindow.cs Validator without Unity tools/content-check/

The game reads the files with Resources.Load<TextAsset>("Content/cards"), which means they also work in a build, not only in the Editor. ContentDatabase loads them once and keeps them in memory; CardLibrary and EnemyLibrary are only facades over it.

docs.title: Two ways to edit
docs.text:
Spreadsheet. Open the CSV with Excel (or LibreOffice), edit it and save it as CSV. The game and the window read it the same way. The separator is detected automatically: ; if Excel is in Catalan or Spanish, , if it is in English. Saving keeps the same separator.

Unity window. Prototype → Content (CSV) menu. It has four tabs, a list on the left and a form on the right, with +, Copy, Delete, Reload from CSV, Save to CSV and Validate buttons. It saves exactly the same files, so you can alternate between the two tools. It has no undo history: if you reload, you lose unsaved changes (the title shows it with a *).

If you save while the game is in Play mode, the cache reloads, but the cards already in the deck or in hand are the old ones: start a new run to see the changes.

docs.title: Table format
docs.text:
The first row is the header. Column names are case-insensitive and their order is free; unknown columns are ignored (and lost when saving).

Effects and intents go in a single cell shaped name:value, separated by | or +:

damage:8|vulnerable:2
attack:11|block:6|attack:7

docs.title: cards.csv
docs.text:
Column Values Notes id [a-z0-9_]+, unique Identity of the card title text What is shown on the card text text, optional If empty, it is generated from the effects cost 0-3 kind attack, skill, power Decides the colour pool starter, reward, both, none Where the card shows up copies integer >= 1 Copies in the starting deck (ignored unless starter/both) effects list of effects 
id;title;text;cost;kind;pool;copies;effects
strike;Strike;;1;attack;starter;4;damage:6
bash;Bash;;2;attack;starter;1;damage:8|vulnerable:2

docs.title: enemies.csv
docs.text:
Column Values Notes id [a-z0-9_]+, unique title text maxhp integer > 0 role normal, pack, boss normal = solo; pack = comes in a group of two; boss = boss intents attack/block list Repeats in a cycle 
id;title;maxhp;role;intents
jaw_worm;Jaw Worm;44;normal;attack:11|block:6|attack:7

The combat room picks like this: 55% one normal enemy; otherwise, two pack enemies (they may repeat). The boss of the final room is drawn from among the boss rows.

docs.title: relics.csv
docs.text:
Column Values id [a-z0-9_]+, unique title text description text rarity common, uncommon, rare, boss, event

Not used yet

The relic system does not exist: the table is a catalogue to have the content written down, but no screen reads it.

docs.title: events.csv
docs.text:
Column Values id [a-z0-9_]+, unique title text text text weight integer > 0 options Label => effect+effect | Other => effect 
id;title;text;weight;options
old_shrine;Old Shrine;A mossy shrine hums.;10;Pray => heal:15 | Desecrate => gain_gold:25+lose_hp:5 | Leave => nothing

Event effects: nothing, heal, lose_hp, gain_gold, lose_gold, max_hp and add_card:card_id (for example add_card:strike).

Not used yet

The event room is still a placeholder. The table and the format are already validated so the content is ready when the screen arrives.

docs.title: Combat effect vocabulary
docs.text:
Effect Aliases Meaning damage attack Damage to the target damage_all all, aoe Damage to every living enemy block defend Player block draw Draw cards gain_energy energy Extra energy this turn vulnerable vuln Applies Vulnerable (x1.5 incoming damage)

Adding a new effect is still code work: EffectKind, the switch in CombatSession.ApplyEffects and, if it is a status, a field in EnemyInstance. The table only gets the new name.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
The same rules apply to the game, the window and the console tool:

  • id unique, lowercase, no accents and no spaces.
  • Title mandatory (and description for relics, text for events).
  • Card cost between 0 and 3; HP, effect values, intents and weights greater than 0.
  • No card without effects; no enemy without intents; no event without options.
  • add_card must point to a card that exists.
  • A warning if the enemy table has no normal, no pack or no boss rows.

If the content has errors, the game does not crash: it loads what it can and writes every problem to the console with the file and the row (cards.csv: row 12: unknown effect 'dammage').

docs.title: Verifying without opening Unity
docs.text:
dotnet run --project tools/content-check

It reads the four tables, validates them, checks that writing and reading back gives the same file and exits with code 1 if there are errors. With the --write argument it rewrites the files in normalised form (useful after editing them by hand).

powershell -File tools/compile-check.ps1 compiles Assets/Scripts and Assets/Editor, so the window is checked too without opening the Editor.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• There are no card ScriptableObjects: you cannot drag them into an Inspector field. If we ever need that, a CSV → .asset importer can be written; today it does not exist on purpose.
  • Unknown columns are lost when saving from the window.
  • The window has no undo; the CSV does have history in git.
  • The id is the identity of the card (and will be for save/continue): changing it afterwards is the same as deleting the card and creating another one.

docs.title: Current gaps
docs.text:
1. Gold is useless — it is displayed and cannot be spent (shop pending).
  2. There is only one effect (Vulnerable) and 10 cards: combat still does not have enough decisions per card. The CSV format is ready to grow without touching code.
  3. The map has to be redesigned. The current radial one (fog + LateralChance) worked, but the shape of the run will be decided with the new map: reveal radius, being able to go back and how many rooms a run should last. The 24.9% dead-end and 11.35 rooms-per-run figures no longer rule.

docs.title: Priorities
docs.text:
Ordered by value / effort ratio:

# What Why Effort 1 Development panel (F1) Makes everything else testable in seconds Low ✅ 2 Deck view + card detail Without it the decisions cannot be evaluated Low ✅ 3 Combat feedback Floating numbers and flashes: changes how it feels Low-mid ✅ 4 Multi-enemy + target selection The biggest jump in depth Mid-high ✅ 5 8 new effects + 15-20 cards Weak, Strength, Dexterity, multi-hit, area… Mid 6 Shop Gives gold a purpose Mid 7 Relics Identity for each run Mid 8 Rest with a choice (heal vs upgrade) Real decisions on the map Low-mid 9 Events Narrative variety Mid 10 Save/continue + manual seed Longer sessions and repeatability Mid 11 AI art and sound Polish (lots of generation time) High

docs.title: Batch 1 — make the prototype observable ✅
docs.text: Dev panel + deck view + combat feedback. It adds no content, but it makes what is already there visible and testable.

docs.title: Batch 2 — make combat interesting
docs.text: Multi-enemy with target selection ✅ + the new effects pack + 15 cards. This is where the game starts to have real decisions.

docs.title: Batch 3 — make the run interesting
docs.text: Shop + relics + rest with a choice. Gold and the map stop being decorative.

docs.title: Batch 2b — information fog on the radial map
docs.text:
The map is radial and the player can walk in both directions. The topology is visible, but room type only reveals itself at distance 1; bosses are always visible. Visited rooms do not repeat content and are used to get back to a branch.

Status (2026-10-28): the playtest works and the fog is accepted. The decisions that were left (provisions, frontier vs. current position, run size) move to the map redesign; they are not closed here.

  • Provisions: if the player explores every branch, make each move consume a provision. Open decision in the new map.
  • Frontier versus current position: for now you can only enter a direct neighbour; nodes connected to other visited rooms are known but cannot be teleported to. It is the point to revisit with "being able to go back".
  • Run size: the LateralChance = 0.55 figures (11.35 rooms per run) stop being the reference; they will be measured on the new map.

docs.title: Playtest questions
docs.text:
To answer with the game in hand:

Combat and rewards (Batch 2 already tested for clicks, targeting and feedback):

  • With 3 energy and 5 cards, do you end combats with energy to spare or unable to do anything?
  • Does a combat last 2-3 turns or 4-6? A normal combat should last 4-6.
  • With 72 HP, do you reach the boss alive or is the map too harsh?
  • Do you always pick the same reward card? If so, the pool is too small.
  • Are the packs (JawWormPack, CultistPack) the right size and damage?

Map (these will be asked again on the new map):

  • Do you end up over-exploring (too many combats) or do you go straight for the boss? How many rooms per run?
  • Do you miss a limit on exploration, or is health enough already?
  • Is the reveal radius generous enough to decide the route, or do you lack information?
  • Does being able to go back make you explore more or give you agency?
  • Zoom (wheel vs. buttons) and how the outer ring reads: these will be sharpened with the new map.

docs.title: 2026-10-21 · Vertical slice
docs.text: Commits: 5ce0f83 (base project) · 700d2a7 (vertical slice)

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Go from a freshly created Unity 6.3 project to a complete playable loop: map, card combat and rewards. A thin vertical slice so we can play something as early as possible.

docs.title: What was done
docs.text:
• Located and configured the existing project (URP 2D, new Input System).
  • Connected the Editor to the agent through the MCP relay (opencode.json).
  • Imported TextMesh Pro Essential Resources (without them nothing compiles).
  • Map Slay the Spire style: 6 floors (5 normal + boss), 7 columns, 4 paths, edges that do not cross, deterministic per seed.
  • Combat turn-based: 3 energy, draw 5 cards, block that resets, Vulnerable ×1.5.
  • Content: 10 cards (Strike, Defend, Bash, Cleave, Pommel Strike, Iron Wave, Shrug It Off, Thunderclap, Heavy Blade, Battle Trance) and 3 enemies (Jaw Worm 44 HP, Cultist 50 HP, The Guardian 90 HP as the boss).
  • Entire UI built from code with UIFactory: no prefabs and no screens assembled in the Editor.
  • Screens: map, combat, reward, rest, placeholder and end of run.
  • Assets/Scenes/Prototype.unity scene with a single Game object.

docs.title: Map simulation
docs.text:
The floor map is deterministic per seed: 4 paths climb from floor 0 to the boss and the edges that would cross are rejected. I ran it through the same benchmark as the two radial maps (see the 2026-10-25 session): 300 seeds × 40 runs = 12,000 traversals, with a player who enters through a random room on floor 0 and then picks a random edge.

Seed 42. Rooms with a dashed outline are the possible entrances; the boss is at the top. Click the image to see it full size.

Metric Value Rooms per map 15.1 Edges per map 16.6 Bosses 1 (always) Rooms with more than one exit 2.3 Edges that cross 0 (worst map: 0) Unreachable or overlapping rooms 0 Traversals that reach the boss 100% Traversals with no way out 0% Rooms per traversal 5.0 (always; 6 counting the entrance)

100% does not mean the map is better: it means there are no direction decisions. Edges only go upwards, every room has at least one and every room on the last floor goes to the boss, so every run follows exactly the same route of 5 rooms. The map is small (15 rooms) because the 4 paths merge immediately: only 2.3 rooms per map offer more than one exit. That is what led us to try the radial map with free movement.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• UGUI + TextMeshPro, not UI Toolkit: it is what the genre asks for and what the reference does.
  • UI from code instead of prefabs: fast iteration and everything versioned as text.
  • Content in C# (CardLibrary) and not in ScriptableObjects yet: changing numbers means editing one line. It will be migrated when the volume grows.
  • A single scene: screens are runtime panels.
  • No movement: the game is a node map + turn-based combat, not a top-down exploration game.

docs.title: Objective

docs.title: Development panel (F1)
docs.text:
Overlay in the bottom-left corner with the current state (seed, HP, deck size, gold, energy) and these buttons:

Button Effect HEAL TO FULL Heals to full (map and combat) ADD RANDOM CARD Adds a card from the reward pool WIN COMBAT Closes the combat as a victory +1 ENERGY Extra energy for the turn SKIP ROOM Skips the current room (or picks a random one on the map) RESTART (SAME SEED) Restarts with the same map RESTART (NEW SEED) New run

docs.text:

docs.title: 2026-10-25 · Radial map: from the star to the rings
docs.text: Duration: afternoon Commits: cf408e4 (radial map) · 231e2cc (rings, more bosses and zoom/pan) · 98b6304 (simulations and docs) · 4bd2079 (room distribution) · 7f00972 (deck wheel)

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Break the rigidity of the floor map: 5 rooms, a single direction and no path decisions. The idea is a radial map with the centre as the entrance, rings of rooms and several bosses on the edge, where you can choose which way to go. And it has to stay readable: no crossings, no edges slicing across the map, and with zoom to see it whole or up close.

docs.title: v2 — the star (cf408e4)
docs.text:
• Start centre, 7 rings (5 room + 1 boss) and rooms growing from 5 to 15 per ring.
  • Free, bidirectional movement: you can enter any neighbouring room without visiting it, inwards or outwards. Visited rooms close. If no unvisited neighbour is left, the end-of-run screen appears (END RUN).
  • Each room on a ring links to the 1-2 rooms closest in distance on the outer ring; those left without a door are picked up in a second pass.
  • 3-6 bosses on the outer ring, one per sector.

The result is much bigger than the floor map (50 rooms), but it does not read: on an ellipse, linking by distance makes many edges tilt and cross (1.4 per map, up to 9), and the boss edges can cross ring 4 again. It looks like a spider web.

docs.title: v3 — the rings (231e2cc)
docs.text:
• Linking by angular wedges: each room on the big ring hangs off the room (or boss) on the small ring that is closest in angle. The map ends up split into wedges centred on the small ring, and two roads from different wedges cannot cross.
  • Rooms on the same ring are joined with arcs that follow the ring, never with a straight line that cuts across it.
  • The ring just before the bosses is a complete ring: from any branch you can go around the map and pick another boss.
  • 4-7 bosses, each on the angular centre of its rooms, so that the edges of the last hop do not leave their ring.
  • LateralChance = 0.5 on rings 1-4; ring 5, just before the bosses, is always complete.
  • Zoom and pan: wheel or +/− buttons (60%-220%), drag with the right or middle button and RESET VIEW. The map is clipped inside its area so it does not cover the HUD.

docs.title: Room distribution (4bd2079)
docs.text:
• 50% combat, 15% rest, 10% shop and 25% event (previously 62/18/10/10). Ring 1 is still always combat.
  • With 40 rolled rooms (rings 2-5) you get about 10 event rooms and 4 shop rooms per map; combats drop from 29.8 to 25.1 per map.
  • Shop and event are still placeholder screens: for now 35% of the rolled rooms have no real content. The distribution is designed for when they do.

docs.title: Bug: the deck wheel moved the map (7f00972)
docs.text:
MapScreen reads the wheel (and the right and middle buttons) directly from Mouse.current, not from the EventSystem. With the deck open, the card scroll also reached the map and zoomed it (and, with the right button, panned it) behind.

  • DeckScreen counts open overlays with a static OpenCount (OnEnable / OnDisable) and MapScreen.Update returns early while there is any.
  • When the deck closes, the counter goes back to 0 and the map recovers wheel and drag.

docs.title: Simulation of the three maps
docs.text:
Same benchmark for the three algorithms: 300 seeds × 40 runs = 12,000 traversals per map. Two runs per seed: one random (picks any unvisited neighbour) and one that always looks outwards (if it can, it climbs a ring). The first measures the map as exploration; the second, as a path to the boss. On the floor map there is no difference because there is only one direction.

Click the images to open them full size.

Seed 42. Linking by distance creates long, crossing edges: 1.4 crossings per map on average, up to 9.

Seed 42. The same kind of map (~50 rooms), now with wedges, arcs and a complete ring before the bosses: 0 crossings across 300 seeds.

Metric v1 · floors v2 · star v3 · rings Rooms per map 15.1 50.5 51.5 Edges per map 16.6 69.0 87.2 Bosses per map 1 3-6 4-7 Rooms with more than one exit 2.3 20.0 9.0 Edges that cross (average) 0 1.44 0 Edges that cross (worst map) 0 9 0 Overlapping rooms or outside the area 0 0 0 Edges passing under another button 0 2.22 0.47 Runs reaching the boss (random) 100% 86.1% 75.1% Runs reaching the boss (always outwards) 100% 100% 100% Dead-end runs (random) 0% 13.9% 24.9% Rooms per run (random) 5.0 7.71 11.35 Rooms per run (outwards) 5.0 6.00 6.00

The run figures do not count the entrance room.

What the numbers say

  • v1 is a corridor, not a map. 15 rooms, 2.3 branching points and always 5 rooms of route. The 100% of runs reaching the boss and the 0% of dead ends are not a design merit: they are the consequence of every edge going upwards and every room having one.
  • v2 triples the map but breaks it. Going from 15 to 50 rooms and from 5 to 7.71 rooms of route is exactly what we were after, but 1.44 crossings per map (up to 9) and 2.22 edges passing under another button mean it cannot be read at a glance. In 222 of 300 maps there is at least one such edge.
  • v3 fixes the drawing and gains exploration. 0 crossings and 11.35 rooms per random run (previously 7.71). The price is that one in four random runs ends in a dead end (24.9%) and that there are fewer rooms with two exits (9.0 against 20.0): every room on the big ring has a single radial door and the network closes with arcs.
  • The dead ends are not the bosses' fault. Always going outwards reaches the boss in 6 rooms 100% of the time. Dead ends appear when the player goes inwards or sideways: lateral connections are the lever (LateralChance).
  • The v3 bosses: 4, 5, 6 or 7 bosses in 72, 72, 82 and 74 of the 300 seeds.
  • One remaining blemish: in v3, in 74 of 300 maps an edge of the last hop passes under a neighbouring room's button. It is because the boss sits at the centre of its wedge and an edge room receives a very steep edge. Since the buttons are drawn on top, only a piece of line disappears; it is purely aesthetic.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Simulation: 300 seeds × 40 runs for the three maps. On v3, 0 crossings (worst map: 0), 0 unreachable rooms, 0 overlaps and 0 rooms outside the area; every benchmark assertion passes.
  • Play mode over MCP: map at 100% and at 176% with zoom and pan; 5 of 5 clicks hit the right room at 176%; the zoom buttons go up and down with a 1.12 factor and RESET VIEW returns to 100%; panning stays limited to the area.
  • A run driven always outwards reaches the boss and shows THE HOLLOW OPENS.
  • Wheel bug: in Play mode, with the deck open (OpenCount = 1), injecting 120 wheel units left the zoom at 106% and the map content at (5.77, -102.96); with the deck closed (OpenCount = 0), the same injection raised the zoom to 118% (1.06 × 1.12). No errors or warnings in the console.
  • The Unity console shows no errors after the commits.
  • Captures in %TEMP%\opencode\unity-shots\ (not committed).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Free, bidirectional movement instead of only outwards: the map is meant to be explored, and going back should not be a punishment. Visited rooms close so that each room has content only once.
  • Dead end = explicit end of run (END RUN), not a silent block. More honest and easier to measure.
  • Angular wedges instead of distance: distance on an ellipse lies (a room can be "closer" to the opposite boss) and generates crossings. Angle is the coordinate that orders the ring and the one that makes the map planar.
  • Arcs for same-ring edges: a straight line between two rooms of the ring cuts the ring and crosses the radial edges; the arc does not.
  • Complete ring before the bosses: it gives one last boss decision without adding any crossing edge.
  • Bosses on the centre of their wedge: it is what stops the edges of the last hop from leaving the ring. The trade-off is that an edge room receives a steep edge that passes under the neighbouring button (0.47 per map).
  • Ellipse 1.45 instead of a circle: makes the most of 16:9 and gives more horizontal separation between rooms.
  • LateralChance as the lever: it is the number that decides how much the player explores and how many dead ends there are; now 0.5.
  • 4-7 bosses (previously 3-6): the outer ring is the last decision; with 4-7 and a complete ring, there is always more than one within reach.
  • A static counter in the deck instead of routing the wheel through the EventSystem: sending zoom to IScrollHandler would be more "correct" in UGUI's eyes, but it would change behaviour across the whole map (the HUD would block scrolling too) and right-button panning is not a UI drag. The counter solves the real case in three lines.

docs.title: 2026-10-27 · External skills from skills.sh
docs.text: Duration: afternoon Commits: 3183de6 — skills: nine skills vendored from the skills.sh catalogue

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Stop writing skills by hand. The engineering and design knowledge we use every session (uGUI, MonoBehaviour lifecycle, Input System, card zones, run economy) is not ours: it exists in public agent skills catalogues. Today's job is to bring it in from outside, versioned in the repo, instead of reinventing it.

docs.title: Method: how they are found and installed
docs.text:
1. The API is closed. https://skills.sh/api/v1/skills/search?q=... returns 401 authentication_required: it wants a Vercel OIDC token. Not an option for a local project.
  2. The web search does work. The https://www.skills.sh/search?q=<term> pages are server-rendered: opening them in a browser shows the whole list (skill, repo, installs). The pages https://www.skills.sh/<owner>/<repo>/<slug> carry the install command and the security audits.
  3. Vendored installation. Instead of npx skills add (which writes to the agent's global folder and does not stay in the repo), the upstream is downloaded and copied to .opencode/skills/<slug>/, with an Upstream source footer.

The full loop, to repeat it whenever a skill needs updating or adding:

# 1. Find the real path inside the repo (routes vary: skills/, skills/unity/, SKILL.md at the root)
Invoke-RestMethod "https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/trees/main?recursive=1" |
  Select-Object -ExpandProperty tree | Where-Object { $_.path -like "*SKILL.md" }

# 2. Download the SKILL.md and the files it references (references/, scripts/)
Invoke-WebRequest "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/main/<path>/SKILL.md" `
  -OutFile ".opencode/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md" -UseBasicParsing

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Vendor, do not install globally. The repo is what has to know what it works with; a global install does not travel between machines and does not stay in the history.
  • The body belongs to upstream. Only the provenance footer is added (repo, path, date, audits) and, if needed, the normalisation of a broken description. Divergences with the project are documented in the project skill, not by editing the external one.
  • When they clash, the project one wins. unity-ugui-code knows the UI is built from code and at 1600×900; ui-ugui assumes prefabs and the Editor. The external ones are general doctrine.
  • Searching outside is step 1. The end-of-session routine in AGENTS.md now says, in this order: search skills.sh for the general knowledge behind the next 1-2 roadmap items; write a project skill only for what upstream cannot know (this repo's numbers, classes, pitfalls and verification); and update the existing ones if the session changed how they work.

docs.title: 2026-10-28 · Content in CSV and session-start context
docs.text: Duration: afternoon Commits: 1cacece feat: author cards, enemies, relics and events from CSV · 3132230 docs: capture the radial map and read the full context at session start · this commit — skills: three design skills for the effect batch

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Two things that looked separate and are not:

  1. Take content out of the code. Adding a card cannot mean creating a ScriptableObject by hand; it should mean writing a row in a spreadsheet.
  2. Not losing context between sessions. The agent only read the newest note, and the Pending items from three sessions ago were never seen.

docs.title: Content pipeline
docs.text:
• Csv.cs — CSV reader and writer with automatic delimiter detection (; for Excel in Catalan/Spanish, , otherwise) and keeping the same delimiter when saving.
  • ContentCsv.cs — the format in a single place: headers with aliases, validation with row numbers, writing and reading the four tables. It is the only definition of the format; neither the runtime nor the editor keeps a copy.
  • ContentDatabase.cs — loading from Resources/Content, cache and Reload(). It is needed because the project has domain reload disabled: GameManager.StartNewRun calls it so a CSV edit shows up without restarting Play.
  • Flat data — CardData and EnemyData stop being ScriptableObject and become [Serializable], so they can be validated outside Unity. RelicData and EventData are added, still without a game system.
  • copies — new column to preserve the starting deck of 4 Strike / 4 Defend.
  • Effects in one cell — damage:8|vulnerable:2, with the card text auto-generated when the text column is empty.
  • Facades — CardLibrary and EnemyLibrary keep the API the game already used (Normal, Pack, Boss(rng)) but read from the CSV.
  • Editor window — Prototype → Content (CSV): tabs per table, add, copy and delete rows, reload, save and validate. It warns if the file changed outside and marks the relic and event tables as inert.
  • tools/content-check — validation and round-trip of the CSVs with dotnet run, without opening Unity. tools/compile-check.ps1 now compiles Assets/Editor too.

docs.title: Documentation and context
docs.text:
• docs/content.md — the format, the effects, the aliases and the workflow.
  • Radial map capture at docs/images/2026-10-28-radial-map.png, inside the morning page.
  • AGENTS.md — the start routine no longer reads only the latest note: it reads index, roadmap, architecture, content, the session index, the three latest notes in full, the Pending sections of every old one and the git log. The reply must quote the pending items, not reconstruct them from memory, and must say so if the roadmap and the latest note contradict each other.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/compile-check.ps1 → 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  • dotnet run --project tools/content-check → 10 cards, 5 enemies, 0 relics, 0 events and Content OK. Error test done: it prints the row and exits with code 1.
  • Unity, Play mode: Deck 9 cards, Rooms 1/65, HP 72/72 and no errors in the fresh console. The 9 cards confirm that copies and loading from the CSV work.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• The CSV is the single source of truth. No .asset files are generated: what is in the spreadsheet is what the game loads, and the Editor window saves to the same file.
  • Flat classes instead of ScriptableObject. They allow validating and round-tripping with dotnet, outside Unity, inside the same repository.
  • The delimiter is detected and preserved. A file saved by Excel in Catalan must not become a comma-separated file that breaks decimal numbers.
  • Effects live in one cell. One column per effect would have made the table grow without limit; the card text generates itself when it is not there.
  • Relics and events exist as a catalogue, not as a system. It is better to have the tables and the editor ready before the code that uses them; the window says so explicitly to avoid selling smoke.
  • The session start reads the whole context. The cost is a bit of reading; the cost of the alternative is repeating work or contradicting a decision from three sessions ago.

docs.title: 2026-10-28 · Map with fog and connections
docs.text: Duration: afternoon Commits: 1fc4e15 feat: tune foggy radial map navigation · 1cacece feat: author cards, enemies, relics and events from CSV · this commit — docs: capture the radial map

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Try a radial map with progressively revealed information, configurable backtracking and more options to switch branches without making the roads unreadable.

docs.title: What was done
docs.text:
• Added fog of war with a configurable reveal radius (1-5).
  • Visibility is cumulative: it is computed from every visited room.
  • Backtracking can now be configured from the F1 panel.
  • The map went from 7 to 8 rings, with one more room before the bosses.
  • Same-ring connections are now straight lines.
  • Connections were adjusted: 55% normal lateral and 35% diagonals between branches of consecutive rings.
  • Connections are validated against crossings and against proximity to the node rectangles; if a radial connection is not safe, an alternative branch is tried.
  • The defaults are fog off and backtracking off.

docs.title: Capture
docs.text: A new run with a random seed, zoom at 100% and fog off (the default). You can see the 8 rings, the straight lateral connections, the diagonals between branches and the four bosses on the outer ring.

  • Diagonals only connect consecutive rings and pick a neighbouring angular branch.
  • Geometric safety is validated during generation, not only while the UI draws.
  • Provisions stay pending until the playtest shows that exploration needs to be limited.
